beats.trigger: ## Building Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new, a title

beats.trigger: A system remembers, grows, and compounds. Chat doesn't.
beats.got: The module is about files that persist, not about chatting better.

beats.trigger: (4) Karpathy's LLM Wiki post. (5) Optional: Lindenberg memory-architecture piece.
beats.got: A reading list with five items, and I'd skip two.

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** whether memory is compounding or growing
beats.got: Nothing new, but 'compounding vs growing' is a useful distinction.

beats.trigger: What's the difference between asking an LLM a question and having an LLM maintain a knowledge base for you?
beats.got: Maintaining a knowledge base is the job, as opposed to asking one-off questions.

beats.trigger: Connectors let the agent combine clues that live apart, like a wiki page and an email thread.
beats.got: The agent can join up scattered sources. That's useful for the pricing pilot.

beats.trigger: The guardrail: propose or draft only, do not send, edit, book, or change anything.
beats.got: A scheduled agent that only drafts is something I could allow in my team.

beats.trigger: Good: *The Q2 pricing redesign: usage-based vs. seats, pilot cohort, sales briefing.*
beats.got: My usage-pricing pilot is the challenge, and a short interview turns it into a brief.

beats.trigger: Keep it narrow enough that 5–8 topic pages cover it.
beats.got: Scope it small, with 5–8 pages.

beats.trigger: If an email thread, deck, or doc feels sensitive, skip it.
beats.got: Start with non-sensitive material. Legal will like that.

beats.trigger: If the agent starts reading before showing it, stop it, steer narrower, say *"continue"*.
beats.got: I can stop the agent and make it show a plan first.

beats.trigger: Push back, sharpen, add what's missing.
beats.got: The agent proposes sources and I correct them. That is how I work with a junior anyway.

beats.trigger: Aim for 8–10 items with real content or local-path links across lists (1) and (2)
beats.got: Aim for 8–10 real sources. The unreachable ones stay on a list.

beats.trigger: give one sentence of feedback and ask for a revised plan.
beats.got: One sentence of feedback gets me a revised plan, so I approve before it writes files.

beats.trigger: That list is your first quality check.
beats.got: The memory can list its own gaps and contradictions. I want to see whether it catches the churn article.

beats.trigger: Citations show whether the agent read the memory or the LLM filled in from training data.
beats.got: Citations are the check that the answer came from my files. My CFO would ask for exactly that.

beats.trigger: Push back if a claim "got sharper" but the top didn't change.
beats.got: A new source should change the page's top line, and I can check that it did.

beats.trigger: Reject the ones that miss; the agent applies the ones you approve.
beats.got: The agent proposes maintenance and I approve or reject each item.

beats.trigger: If it is generic or leans on uncited knowledge, that shows where the memory is still thin.
beats.got: A hard question tests the memory. A vague or uncited answer shows where it's thin.

beats.trigger: A system is *persistence* (files it reads again) plus *automation* (it runs).
beats.got: Files plus a running agent make a system.

beats.trigger: The second batch made the first batch better.
beats.got: New sources improved the old pages, not just added to them.

beats.trigger: A saved document with no agent is just a document. An agent with no files is a chat.
beats.got: nothing new. This repeats the previous slide.

beats.trigger: old and new claims met and the ones that couldn't survive got cut.
beats.got: The existing pages go into the prompt, so old and new claims collide and the weak ones get cut.

beats.trigger: Keep the rules small and boring.
beats.got: Small, boring rules applied consistently.

beats.trigger: No database, special tool or paid tier is needed.
beats.got: It's just markdown files. That's cheap, and I could share the folder with my team.

beats.trigger: Sharpen the memory, never the sources, or you lose the evidence.
beats.got: Keep the originals untouched and edit only the memory layer.

beats.trigger: *Generic AI becomes your AI when you build the memory it reads.*
beats.got: nothing new. It's a slogan version of the last two slides.

beats.trigger: If a competitor could claim a page, the memory is growing but not compounding.
beats.got: A page a competitor could have written is a weak page. That's a test I can apply to my pricing memory.

beats.trigger: Most of what you know about your company sits in heads and corridors, and nobody has written it down.
beats.got: The agent only knows what is written down, and most of my team's knowledge isn't.

beats.trigger: The agent writes the rules file from the session: what worked, what rubbed, what got repeated.
beats.got: The session produces a first rules file that I can edit.

beats.trigger: What the agent leaves out is often the signal.
beats.got: Check what the summary skipped, because the messy bits are often the point.

beats.trigger: Every miss turns into a line of context that stops the next miss.
beats.got: When the output is wrong, fix the context or rule, not just the prompt.

beats.trigger: The model will change under this. The memory will not.
beats.got: The folder is the durable asset, so it survives a model swap.

take_homes: Keep the pricing-pilot sources in one folder of markdown files, with an agent that reads them and cites them. That folder is the asset, and it keeps its value across tools.
Ask the memory a hard question and check every claim has a citation. A vague or uncited answer shows where the memory is thin.
When the output is wrong, fix the memory or the rule file instead of rewriting the prompt.

monday.move: Start the usage-pricing memory: write challenge.md, pull 8-10 sources including the Q2 review and the churn article, and have the agent flag where they disagree
monday.who: me, then show two people from my team of fourteen
monday.stop_condition: The agent's answer to 'where does the pilot plan break' cites sources and tells me something I didn't know. If it stays generic, I stop.
monday.blocker: There is no shared place for the context files. My folder would be a private copy again.

misconception.why: A new source made existing pages sharper and changed their top line with no change to my prompt. That is a different lever from better prompts. I still expect prompt quality to matter, so it's shaken and not changed.

one_line: Good hands-on hour, and the folder it leaves you is what's worth keeping, but the middle slides repeat themselves and the team-sharing question is left open.
